\begin{bankpassage}[id=SI26-P1-CHEM-S2-G7-8, source={Score-I - Test 26 (18 Dec 2022)}, questions={7-8}]
The wave function for an atomic orbital of single electron atom or ion is
\[\begin{aligned}\Psi(r,\theta,\phi)={}&\frac{2}{3}\left(\frac{Z}{3a_0}\right)^{3/2}(1-\sigma)\\&\times(12-8\sigma+\sigma^2)\,\sigma\, e^{-\sigma/2}\cos\theta.\end{aligned}\]
Where $\sigma=\dfrac{2Zr}{na_0}$, $a_0=0.529$ \AA.

All other parameters have their usual meaning.
\end{bankpassage}

(i) $\psi_r = 2\left(\dfrac{1}{a_0}\right)^{3/2} e^{-r/na_0}$\par

\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}

\begin{bankpassage}[id=SRGBT02-P1-CHEM-S1-G31-32, source={SRGBT - Test 02 (01 Aug 2021)}, questions={31-32}]
Both de--Broglie hypothesis and Heisenberg uncertainty principle establish that microscope particles have more prominent wave nature.\par
Heisenberg realised that, in the world of very small particles one cannot measure any property of a particle without interacting with it in some way. This introduces an unavoidable uncertainty into the result. One can never measure all the properties exactly.\par
Minimum uncertainty in position of any body is given by wavelength of light.\par
\textbf{Heisenberg's uncertainty principle :}\par
$\Delta\mathrm x\;.\;\Delta\mathrm P\;\geq\;\dfrac{\mathrm h}{4\pi}=\dfrac{\hbar}2$\par
(uncertainty in position, uncertainty in momentum)\par
\textbf{De--Broglie hypothesis :}\par
$\lambda=\dfrac{\mathrm h}{\mathrm P}$\par
where $\lambda$ is de--Broglie wavelength of any body having non relativistic momentum P.
\end{bankpassage}

A gas of identical H-like atom has some atoms in the lowest (ground) energy level A and few atoms in a particular upper (excited) energy level B and there are no atoms in any other energy level. The atoms of the gas make transition to a higher energy level by absorbing monochromatic light of photon energy 2.7 eV. Subsequently, the atoms emit radiation of only six different photons energies. Some of the emitted photons have energy 2.7 eV. Some have more and some have less than 2.7 eV. How many statements is/are correct ?\par
(i) \quad The principal quantum number of initially excited level B = 2.\par
(ii) \quad The ionisation energy for the gas atoms is 28.8 eV.\par
(iii) \quad The maximum and the minimum energies of the emitted photons will be 13.5 eV and 0.699 eV respectively.\par
(iv) \quad In above question nucleus is stationary \& e$^-$ will revolve around the nucleus in circular path.\par
(v) \quad If all emitted photons have energy $\ge$ 2.7 eV, then in this case principal quantum number of initially excited level B = 3.
\end{bankq}
